title: Asynchronous Multiplayer
author: RoundTableTTRPG
selftext:
I'm not really designing games for people to play, I have joked about the by-line "games for people who hate their friends" for a long time. My game designs are usually a sort of thought or experiment on a subject.

So today I present my thoughts on MMOs.

The opportunity is that multiplayer servers are very expensive computationally and wallet-ly. So I wanted to design a multiplayer server that is always online, always has people online (even when the community is super small), doesn't feel empty, and also runs on the free tier of just about any shared server system.

I present: Kobold Flight Club. Instead of sending data back and forth to the server every tic and trying to synchonize hundreds of players at once, your own browser logs your own run individually and then if you beat the high score sends that to the server once, so 155kb every 2 minutes if you win, or 0 if you don't. To start chaging money to the Blaze tier of the Google studio, I would need more than 10 000 users to boot up at once, drawing all the champion race data simultaneously.

Meanwhile, championship runs are run as ghosts in the old arcade and console racing game style, but with full physics, allowing you to run against and interact with players whether or not they are online at that time.

Give it a try, see if you can get onto the leaderboard

[https://kobold-flight-club.ai.studio/](https://kobold-flight-club.ai.studio/)

Also please post your own game and discussion about how you are handling multiplayer!

comments.author: MightyBig-Dev
comments.body: Yea I built an async game as well because live multiplayer made no sense. Especially when you’re just starting out and don’t have players.

replies.author: RoundTableTTRPG
replies.body: What was the game premise? How did the asynch work?

replies.author: MightyBig-Dev
replies.body: It’s still super early but the game is called rope ninja. It’s a skill based racing game. So when a player versus it finds a player near your ELO and you race them 1v1. If you’d like to see it in action I can drop the web demo link. It’s desktop only.

replies.author: RoundTableTTRPG
replies.body: yeah sure, I'd love to check it out

replies.author: MightyBig-Dev
replies.body:
Keep in mind it’s early. [Rope Ninja Demo](http://ninja.mightybig.ca).   
If you’d check out the leaderboard you can watch a ghost.  Or you can play versus and race a ghost 1v1. I JUST added a learn mode and nobody has tried it, maybe you can take that for a spin first and see if it’s helpful in learning the game.

replies.author: RoundTableTTRPG
replies.body:
Nah man this is awesome. Well done!  
I did the learning mode, it does work, but I am personally anti-tutourial.   
Simple, clean, looks good. You did a good job unifying the aesthetics and all that. Love it.

Tell me a little bit about your workflow, etc

replies.author: MightyBig-Dev
replies.body: Ah thanks!  You’re like the 5th person to play it, but initial feedback was it’s too hard. So I put that tutorial in. Workflow is codex do as I command. lol. But seriously it’s just a lot of iteration and tidying things up as I go. I’m going to release it on steam but have zero expectations for it. Hopefully make my $100 few back would be a win.  I don’t use anything special like skills or other ai dev tools, purely chatting with codex and making something I wanted to play.

replies.author: RoundTableTTRPG
replies.body: For sure it's too hard. And the tutourial will not help. People don't take the time to memorize platformer patterns anymore, and unfortunately I don't think there is much of a solution for that for your game. It is definitely part of the nostalgia and charm. It's like writing a good technical modern classical piano piece. Just because you did it correctly and well doesn't bring the audience back. For what it's worth, this game would have kicked ass in the 80s and early 90s.

replies.author: MightyBig-Dev
replies.body: Aha yea you’re not wrong. This game is actually a love letter to my favourite game and mode in worms 2.  It’s all good, it’s just for me to have fun with any remaining quota on my pro account before a reset lmao. Thanks for taking a look. ✌️😎
